Job Description
As a PFA Engineer Intern on the Yield Enhancement (YE) team, you will support physical failure analysis investigations of defect issues found by YE and Fab customers. You will learn to isolate, expose, and image physical defects in advanced memory devices, analyze the results to help find the root cause, and present clear findings to engineering partners. Alongside your daily work in the lab, you will complete a focused improvement project during the 3-month internship and present the results at the end. You will set your priorities following the YE PFA queue, with guidance from a mentor engineer.

Responsibilities and Tasks

Physical Failure Analysis and Investigation

- Performs PFA sample preparation and analysis (e.g., deprocessing/delayering, cross-sectioning, FIB, SEM/TEM imaging) according to area skill guidelines.
- Reviews EFA results, fault isolation data, and probe/yield data to decide where to target the physical analysis.
- Identifies and categorizes physical defect signatures using defect references, and helps characterize new or unknown defect types.
- Performs data analysis to back up PFA results in pursuit of root cause.
- Summarizes findings in clear, concise reports (images, defect location, likely root cause) and communicates them to part owners and YE/Fab engineers.

Lab Equipment Operation

- Learns to operate PFA lab equipment safely and efficiently, following defined safety and contamination-control guidelines.
- Builds an understanding of how the equipment works and supports basic troubleshooting with equipment owners.

Internship Project and Continuous Improvement

- Owns a focused, short-term project that fits a 3-month timeline and presents the outcome to the team and leadership at the end of the internship.
- Completes all required safety and equipment training certifications defined by area guidelines.
- Builds technical knowledge of device structure, process flow, and failure mechanisms for current and future parts.
- Suggests improvements for the department and participates in team projects that support department and company objectives.

AI-Enabled Analysis and Productivity

- Uses approved AI and digital productivity tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot) to work more efficiently on data analysis, image/report generation, knowledge retrieval, and problem-solving.
- Uses AI tools to speed up documentation, communication, and investigation workflows while keeping data accurate and applying engineering judgment.
- Uses AI technologies responsibly, following company policies, data protection requirements, and intellectual property safeguards.

Schedule
3-month full-time internship, day shift (Monday–Friday).

Education
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, Physics, Chemical Engineering, or a related field.

Qualifications

- Basic understanding of semiconductor devices and fabrication processes.
- Hands-on lab experience is a plus (e.g., microscopy, SEM/FIB, sample preparation, cleanroom).
- Strong attention to detail and good analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Clear written and verbal communication; able to summarize technical results simply.
- Familiarity with data tools (Excel, JMP, Python, etc.) is preferred.

Experience
No prior industry experience required. Previous internships or research projects in semiconductor or failure analysis are preferred.

Meter is a vertically integrated networking company. Hardware, software, services, ISP, and autonomous networks run on a single data pipeline, from the local network to the data center.

Most of the networking industry treats hardware as a commodity–we don’t. Build the hardware right, and everything above it gets better. Meter designs its own Firewalls, Switches, Wireless Access Points, PDUs, and Gateways because customers subscribe to the network instead of buying individual boxes; we're accountable for how the hardware performs for years. We sweat details most people never see, like the logo stamped inside the enclosure and the sound spec on our fans. Great hardware takes more than designing circuits and shipping products: It means thinking hard about performance, reliability, manufacturability, supply chain, installation, sustainability, and the full product lifecycle.

We’re hiring Hardware Engineering Interns to solve real technical problems across Meter’s hardware engineering and operations teams. Over 12 weeks, you’ll own a well-scoped project picked to fit your interests, your experience, and the problems that matter most to Meter:

- Next-generation power adapters: Prototype compact, efficient power supplies that could ship in future Meter products.

- Hardware lifecycle and sustainability: Figure out how Meter hardware can be refurbished, reused, or recycled, and what it takes to extend its life.

- Installer tooling: Build tools, fixtures, or diagnostic devices that make Meter networks faster to install and troubleshoot.

- Acoustics and thermal systems: Design quiet, efficient cooling for future high-performance networking and data center products.

- Supply chain intelligence: Use component and supplier data to spot risks and bottlenecks before they hit a hardware build.

What success looks like

You’ll take a meaningful hardware problem from an open question to a recommendation backed by evidence, and leave behind something the hardware team can use: data, prototypes, test results, engineering requirements, supplier evaluations, or tools.

Your day-to-day will depend on your project, but you may:

- Design, build, and test electrical or mechanical prototypes for future Meter products

- Evaluate components, technologies, architectures, materials, and suppliers

- Write test plans and characterize performance, reliability, thermals, acoustics, power, and other system-level behavior

- Work with our manufacturing partners in Taiwan to understand their capabilities, constraints, cost, and scalability

- Present your findings and recommendations to the hardware team at the end of the internship

Who you are

You’re curious, hands-on, and you learn by building. You’re a good fit if:

- You’re pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical field

- You like taking an ambiguous technical problem and breaking it into questions you can answer through engineering and experimentation

- You’ve built, tested, debugged, or taken apart hardware on a design team, in a lab, or at home, or you’re eager to start

- You’re comfortable working with physical systems: PCBAs, mechanical assemblies, test equipment, prototypes, manufacturing data, or supplier samples

- You can explain technical findings clearly and turn your work into recommendations others can act on

Experience with PCB design, CAD, embedded systems, thermal design, or data analysis is a plus, but none of it is required.

Above all, we’re looking for people who want to understand how great hardware gets built.

Why Meter?

The internet runs the world. Every purchase you make and every video call you join is packets moving through networks. But those networks haven’t changed in decades. They’re brittle, complex, and surprisingly hard to set up for a business.

We started Meter to build better networks, and that meant building everything ourselves: our own enterprise hardware, intuitive software, and streamlined operations. Today we deploy those networks at scale. Bridgewater, Lyft, Reddit, and the San Antonio Spurs rely on Meter to keep thousands of employees and locations online.

Our bet is simple: Everyone will use the internet more than they do today. Meter is building the networking stack that makes connectivity as easy and reliable as water or electricity.

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our silicon teams develop complex digital products where power, performance, area, timing, physical implementation, and manufacturability must come together reliably.

The opportunity

Join the Physical Design team and gain hands-on experience taking a digital design from RTL handoff through physical implementation and signoff. You’ll learn how physical design methodology and flow infrastructure turn design intent into an efficient, manufacturable layout while helping improve repeatability, productivity, and design quality.

This internship is designed for someone who enjoys both engineering fundamentals and practical problem-solving: running a flow, reading timing and QoR reports, investigating a broken stage, adjusting constraints or configuration, and measuring the effect of an iteration. You’ll work with experienced physical design, CAD, front-end, STA, EMIR, and physical-verification engineers on a meaningful project.

What you’ll do

- Learn the physical design flow, development environment, project structure, tools, and methodology needed to contribute effectively.

- Run an assigned block through the RTL-to-signoff flow, including synthesis, floorplanning, power planning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, optimization, timing closure, and signoff.

- Review physical design inputs such as RTL or netlists, SDC constraints, technology files, libraries, LEF/tech files, QRC data, and PDK-related inputs.

- Analyze timing, area, utilization, congestion, clock skew, insertion delay, transition, DRC, LVS, EMIR, and other quality-of-result reports.

- Help identify and resolve flow, implementation, timing, congestion, physical-verification, or infrastructure issues with guidance from experienced engineers.

- Support PPA exploration by running controlled experiments, comparing configurations, tracking results, and documenting the tradeoffs between power, performance, and area.

- Work with physical-design flow configuration, scripts, experiment definitions, reports, logs, and reproducible work areas.

- Contribute to CAD and flow infrastructure improvements such as report generation, run orchestration, validation checks, log mining, root-cause analysis, or handoff packaging.

- Use tools and flows such as Fusion, Innovus, PrimeTime, Calibre, Voltus, or related EDA environments under engineering guidance.

- Collaborate with front-end design, synthesis, STA, EMIR, physical verification, and other teams on inputs, handoffs, signoff criteria, and issue resolution.

- Participate in design reviews, code or flow reviews, technical discussions, issue tracking, documentation, and project planning.

- Deliver assigned physical-design work in a reproducible, well-documented state and present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.

What you bring

- Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, VLSI, or a related field.

- Foundational understanding of digital logic, RTL, CMOS/ASIC design, computer architecture, timing, or semiconductor manufacturing.

- Interest in the physical implementation of digital designs and how layout decisions affect power, performance, area, timing, congestion, and manufacturability.

- Experience with Linux, command-line tools, source control, or scripting through coursework, projects, research, or prior experience.

- A methodical approach to debugging: understand the inputs, reproduce the issue, inspect reports and logs, test a focused change, and evaluate the result.

- Ability to learn unfamiliar tools and technical concepts, ask focused questions, communicate progress and blockers, and follow through on commitments.

- Self-motivation, professionalism, ownership, and a collaborative mindset.

Helpful experience

- ASIC physical design, synthesis, floorplanning, placement, CTS, routing, timing closure, physical verification, or EMIR.

- Static timing analysis, multi-mode/multi-corner concepts, clock constraints, setup/hold analysis, slack, skew, or useful skew.

- Power planning, standard-cell placement, macro placement, congestion analysis, DRC/LVS, antenna checks, or power-integrity analysis.

- Tcl, Python, Bash, YAML, or other scripting and configuration languages used to automate engineering workflows.

- Synopsys Fusion Compiler, Cadence Innovus, PrimeTime, Calibre, Voltus, or comparable EDA tools.

- Git, Bitbucket, P4, Slurm, Snakemake, or other tools used for reproducible, compute-intensive engineering flows.

- Experience comparing QoR across experiments, generating reports, visualizing trends, or debugging flow infrastructure.
